correctness.rationale: The stationary mass identity forces the effective birth factor t<1. For t<1 a convergent resolvent reduces all positive summable equilibria exactly to a finite Perron problem. The explicit biased-walk Green kernel yields a positive matrix similar to K_S=(s^{distance}); strict positivity and monotonicity prove existence/uniqueness and the sharp mortality threshold including equality. Entrywise Perron strictness makes consecutive positions uniquely optimal. The verified tridiagonal inverse yields theta_k=pi/k+O(\(k^{-2}\)), giving limit 2sqrt(pq) and exact pi^2sqrt(pq)/k^2 deficit. At criticality local masses vanish by the Green formula while total equilibrium mass tends 1-1/lambda. A standalone standard-library checker passed Green recurrences, small-matrix Perron roots, exact two-island inequalities, equilibrium residuals and asymptotics.

value.rationale: A natural ecological question asks how many and where low-mortality traits are required to counteract a consistent mutational bias. The result gives a complete arbitrary-finite-layout persistence threshold, proves strict optimality of contiguous traits, sharp \(k^{-2}\) diminishing returns and a universal no-finite-cluster ceiling. The exact two-site example shows rescue at separation at most two but failure from distance three onward; critically, the total population remains positive while a summable trait equilibrium disappears, exposing an important distinction between demographic mass and localization.
